games.title: Language Choice
games.description: Choose the form that makes the unit language accurate.

rounds.prompt: Teacher Yasmin says the attic rule is not a choice. Which sentence states an obligation?
choices: You might wear gloves in the attic.
You could wear gloves in the attic.
You have to wear gloves in the attic.
You would like to wear gloves in the attic.
rounds.answer: You have to wear gloves in the attic.
rounds.explanation: Have to states an obligation, while might and could only state a possibility.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence compares three or more storms correctly?
choices: A tornado spins faster than a storm.
A tornado is the fastest storm of all.
A tornado spins more fast than a storm.
A tornado is more faster than a storm.
rounds.answer: A tornado is the fastest storm of all.
rounds.explanation: The superlative the fastest compares one thing with every other, while faster compares only two.

rounds.prompt: In the Year 4 Exhibition brief, how long must each learner's talk last?
rounds.answer: Two minutes.
rounds.explanation: Part 3 of the brief fixes the talk at two minutes, which is why speakers slow down rather than add pages.

games.title: Reading Detective
games.description: Use unit evidence to solve each reading clue.

rounds.prompt: What did Teacher Yasmin place on every desk, and what did she tell the class to choose?
choices: She placed one thick blue folder on every desk, and she told the class to choose the six pages that carry their own English voice.
The pages must come from at least five different units, and the set must show reading, writing, speaking and new words.
She offers to let that learner present to her alone on Thursday, with nobody else in the room.
rounds.answer: She placed one thick blue folder on every desk, and she told the class to choose the six pages that carry their own English voice.
rounds.explanation: Review the unit text evidence: She placed one thick blue folder on every desk, and she told the class to choose the six pages that carry their own English voice.

rounds.prompt: According to Part 3 of the brief, what three things does a speaker do during the two-minute talk, and in what order?
choices: The pages must come from at least five different units, and the set must show reading, writing, speaking and new words.
She is most proud of page four, because she wrote it twice and the second time was far better.
The speaker opens with their name, then presents three pages, then answers two questions from the audience.
rounds.answer: The speaker opens with their name, then presents three pages, then answers two questions from the audience.
rounds.explanation: Review the unit text evidence: The speaker opens with their name, then presents three pages, then answers two questions from the audience.

rounds.prompt: What does Teacher Yasmin offer a learner who feels too nervous to present on Friday?
choices: It taught her to ask one question and then stop talking.
She offers to let that learner present to her alone on Thursday, with nobody else in the room.
The speaker opens with their name, then presents three pages, then answers two questions from the audience.
rounds.answer: She offers to let that learner present to her alone on Thursday, with nobody else in the room.
rounds.explanation: Review the unit text evidence: She offers to let that learner present to her alone on Thursday, with nobody else in the room.

games.title: Question Quest
games.description: Read each unit question carefully and choose the best answer.

rounds.prompt: Omar sorts letters and parcels at the post counter every morning. What is he sorting?
rounds.answer: the mail
rounds.explanation: Mail is the Unit 1 word for letters and packages that are sent or delivered.

rounds.prompt: Which sentence uses the past simple correctly after the helper did?
choices: Yesterday we did not built the display board.
Yesterday we did not build the display board.
Yesterday we not build the display board.
Yesterday we does not build the display board.
rounds.answer: Yesterday we did not build the display board.
rounds.explanation: The helper did already carries the past, so the main verb stays in its plain form.

rounds.prompt: Complete the question tag: We are presenting on Friday, ______
rounds.answer: aren't we?
rounds.explanation: The sentence is positive and uses are with we, so the tag flips to the negative aren't we.

games.title: Unit Mission
games.description: Finish with a mixed challenge across the whole unit.

rounds.prompt: Nora touched the damp grass and said the ground was still wet. Which review word names that water?
rounds.answer: moisture
rounds.explanation: Moisture is the small amount of water sitting in the air or on a surface, as Unit 2 taught.

rounds.prompt: The horse ran fast on four legs across the field. Which verb describes exactly what it did?
rounds.answer: galloped
rounds.explanation: Gallop is the Unit 5 verb for running fast on four legs; proceed only means to keep going.

rounds.prompt: Amal was not sure that her attic list was good enough to keep. Which word describes her?
rounds.answer: doubtful
rounds.explanation: Doubtful means not sure that something is true or good, which is milder than terrified.
